solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Colin Powell ultimately troubled by new president

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed or thrown into disorder, so the letters of Colin are rearranged
ultimately points to the final letter of the word Powell

explanation.surface: Colin Powell, the American statesman, is worried by an incoming president.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pairs two real US political figures; Colin is not the general here but simply letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Abraham Lincoln was the sixteenth holder of the top US office.

clue.text: At speed, Liverpool footballing legend shift direction slightly

indicators.note: a small change of position for one letter, nudging it along by one place

parts.note: Ian Rush is the Welsh striker who was Liverpool's record goalscorer

explanation.surface: A famous Liverpool striker quickly changes course on the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: Ian Rush was Liverpool FC's record goalscorer; moving one letter of his name one place gives the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something hurriedly or quickly is doing it in a rush.

clue.text: Get excited about author's third chapter on Kindle

parts.note: CA, short for circa, means about

indicators.note: the third letter of the word author

parts.note: to kindle is to set fire to

explanation.surface: A reader gets enthusiastic about a writer's latest chapter on an e-reader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kindle' looks like Amazon's e-reader, but it is the verb to set alight.
explanation.definitionFit: To become suddenly enthusiastic or animated is figuratively to burst into flame.

clue.text: Disembark docked ship in Scottish town

indicators.note: docked means having its tail cut, so the final letter goes

parts.note: to land is to disembark from a ship or plane
the ark is Noah's ship

explanation.surface: Passengers leave a moored vessel in a town in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'docked' suggests a ship in port, but it means cutting the tail off LAND.
explanation.definitionFit: Lanark is a historic market town in South Lanarkshire, Scotland.

clue.text: Ground rules? Expect the worst!

definitions.meaning: sod is turf or ground, so the rules of the ground are playfully its law
the maxim that if something can go wrong it will

explanation.surface: A sports official reads out the rules of play and warns everyone to brace for disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: SOD is turf, i.e. ground, so 'Ground rules' is read as the law belonging to the sod.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverbial principle that whatever can go wrong will go wrong tells you to anticipate misfortune.

clue.text: Veteran general finally laid to rest in blood-stained flag

parts.note: a veteran is old

indicators.note: laid to rest in means placed inside, so one letter goes within the other word

parts.note: gory means covered in blood

indicators.note: finally takes the closing letter of the word general

explanation.surface: An old commander is buried wrapped in a bloodied banner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laid to rest in' puts L, the end of 'general', inside GORY.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Glory is the nickname for the Stars and Stripes, the US national banner.

clue.text: Score three times after team goes up through pen?

indicators.note: through means passing inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means reading the word backwards

parts.note: XI is eleven, the size of a football or cricket team

explanation.surface: A footballer nets a hat-trick after the side climbs up, perhaps from a penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Score' looks like goals but is the number twenty; XI is the usual crossword team.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is twenty, so three of them make the number threescore.

clue.text: University archives accepted regular publications

indicators.note: accepted means taken in, so one letter goes inside

parts.note: annals are historical records or archives

explanation.surface: A university's records department took in some periodicals.
explanation.definitionFit: Annuals are yearbooks, publications that appear once every twelve months.

clue.text: Swallow having drained last of drink

indicators.note: drained of its last means the final letter of the drink is emptied away

parts.note: a martini is a cocktail of gin and vermouth

explanation.surface: Someone gulps down a cocktail until the glass is empty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swallow' looks like a verb about drinking, but it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The house martin and sand martin are birds of the swallow family.

clue.text: Listing names of latest dead before making sign of the cross?

parts.note: the latest thing is what is in, i.e. fashionable
D is the abbreviation for dead, as in genealogies
marking with an X, the cross sign, is X-ing, written here as EXING

explanation.surface: Someone reads out the newly dead, then crosses themselves in prayer.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark covers the liberty of writing X-ing as EXING, putting a cross mark against something.
explanation.definitionFit: Compiling an alphabetical register of names, as at the back of a book, is building an index.

clue.text: Ave Maria he'd transcribed into American idiom

indicators.note: transcribed means written out again in another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A musician arranges the Ave Maria in an American style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transcribed' sounds musical, but it rearranges the letters of AVE MARIA HE'D.
explanation.definitionFit: Martin Luther King's 1963 speech phrase has become a familiar American catchphrase.

clue.text: A quiet wood

parts.note: SH is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: A peaceful forest.
explanation.definitionFit: Ash is a hard pale timber from the tree of that name.

clue.text: Regularly loud — the leader of reform

definitions.text: Regularly loud — the leader of reform

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the word loud, the first and third
the leader of a word is its opening letter, here of reform

explanation.surface: A churchman who was persistently outspoken led the movement for reform.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes Martin Luther, the vocal leader of the Protestant Reformation.
explanation.definitionFit: Martin Luther was the German monk who led the Protestant Reformation, often noisily.

clue.text: O'Malley catches the essence of this?

definitions.text: O'Malley catches the essence of this?

indicators.note: the essence is the inner part, so the letters lie within the words O'Malley catches

explanation.surface: O'Malley, the street-wise feline of Disney's The Aristocats, captures the spirit of his kind.
explanation.walkthrough: O'Malley is the stray tomcat in Disney's The Aristocats, so the clue is also a description of him.
explanation.definitionFit: A stray town feline living rough in back streets is an alley cat, as O'Malley is.

clue.text: Shock announcement in London — one's to inherit the throne!

indicators.note: a Cockney Londoner drops the H when saying the word, so it comes out spoken as AIR

parts.note: a shock is a thick mass of hair

explanation.surface: A startling royal proclamation in the capital names a new successor.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney speech drops the H, so the word for a shock of locks comes out as 'air', which is how the answer is said.
explanation.definitionFit: The person next in line to receive a title or crown is its successor in waiting.

clue.text: Spook finds fault hacking into dodgy site

indicators.note: hacking into means breaking inside, so one piece goes within the other
dodgy means unreliable or crooked, so the letters of site are rearranged

parts.note: an error is a fault or mistake

explanation.surface: A spy discovers a flaw by breaking into a suspicious website.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spook' looks like a spy, a noun, but it is the verb to frighten; 'dodgy' makes TISE.
explanation.definitionFit: To spook someone is to frighten them, a verb sense matching filling with fear.

clue.text: Farting about after class — make to join again

indicators.note: after means the anagram follows the other piece

parts.note: RE, Religious Education, is a school class in Britain

indicators.note: about means moved around, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Schoolchildren fool around after a lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: RE (Religious Education) is a school subject in Britain. INGRAFT is an old spelling of ENGRAFT.
explanation.definitionFit: To graft tissue or a plant shoot back on once more is to reattach it.

clue.text: Commemorative note (foreign currency)

parts.note: a memo is a short written note
the rial is the currency of Iran and other states

explanation.surface: A souvenir message written in foreign money.
explanation.definitionFit: Memorial as an adjective means serving to preserve the memory of someone.

clue.text: Doctor paced around relentlessly in island republic

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters surround the other piece
to doctor is to tamper with or alter, so the letters of paced are rearranged

parts.note: ever can mean always or constantly

explanation.surface: A physician walks back and forth without stopping somewhere in an island nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a physician, but it is the verb to tamper with, signalling the rearrangement to CAPED.
explanation.definitionFit: Cape Verde is an Atlantic archipelago nation off the coast of West Africa.

clue.text: In the manner of the president, dropping round in a state

parts.note: a la, from French, means in the style of

indicators.note: dropping means letting go of a piece, so letters are removed

parts.note: Barack Obama was US president when this was set
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Copying the president's style, someone tours a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Alabama is one of the fifty constituent members of the United States.

clue.text: Piece of card

definitions.meaning: a chessman, the most important on the board
a court card in a pack, ranking above the queen

explanation.definitionFit: The monarch is both a chessman and a picture card in a standard pack.

clue.text: Leaving out duck foie gras over source of heat

indicators.note: leaving out means a letter is omitted from the fodder
over can mean upset or knocked over, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nil, written O

explanation.surface: A cook skips the duck and puts the goose liver over a flame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' looks like the bird behind foie gras, but it is O, the zero.
explanation.definitionFit: A gas-burning heater in a living room is a domestic heating appliance.

clue.text: A bit of Bergerac is terrific for proponent of B&W crime drama

indicators.note: a bit of means only part of the words is taken, sitting within Bergerac is terrific

explanation.surface: A fan praises an episode of Bergerac, the Jersey-set TV detective series, as a black-and-white crime classic.
explanation.walkthrough: Bergerac was a 1980s BBC detective drama set on Jersey. B&W here means black and white people, so a racist promotes a crime of colour prejudice.
explanation.definitionFit: A bigot advocating hostility between black and white people backs a crime of prejudice.

clue.text: Pet shop takes in a mongrel that's forlorn

indicators.note: a mongrel is of mixed breed, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A pet shop adopts a scruffy dog that looks miserable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mongrel' looks like the dog the shop takes in, but it signals mixing the letters of PET SHOP and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Forlorn can mean hopeless, beyond any chance of rescue or recovery.

clue.text: Last to leave the entrance of rehab having taken two drugs or more?

indicators.note: the last letter goes away from the word the
the entrance of a word is its opening letter, here of rehab
two means the drug letter appears twice

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A patient leaving a clinic took a couple of drugs, maybe more.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads off 'two': a number that is two or more is the one after it.
explanation.definitionFit: The number after two is one more than a pair, the figure meant by 'two or more'.

clue.text: Gold rush for part of the year

parts.note: AU is the chemical symbol for gold
a gust is a sudden rush of wind

explanation.surface: A gold rush takes place during one season of the year.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the eighth month of the calendar, a portion of the twelve.

clue.text: Car crashes round bend

indicators.note: a car that crashes is wrecked, so its letters are scrambled; the reversed run inside this word is a coincidence

parts.note: taken as written; the run of letters across Car crashes is a coincidence, not a hidden word

explanation.surface: A motorist comes off the road at a curve.
explanation.definitionFit: An arc is a curved line, a section of a circle's circumference.

clue.text: Cleaner is given introduction to major belief system

parts.note: Fairy is a well-known British brand of washing-up liquid

indicators.note: the introduction to a word is its opening letter, here of major

explanation.surface: A domestic help is introduced to an important philosophy.
explanation.walkthrough: Fairy is a British washing-up liquid brand, so 'Cleaner' is a product, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairyism is belief in the existence of the little folk, a creed of sorts.

clue.text: European club wanting a new kind of signing

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so letters are taken out of the nationality

parts.note: an Italian is a European
C is the card-game abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: A continental football club misses out on a fresh signing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'signing' looks like a transfer deal, but here it means handwriting.
explanation.definitionFit: Italic is a sloping style of handwriting, so one way of writing a signature.

clue.text: Can Pelé lob? Ultimately each shot produces speechless manager?

indicators.note: the final letter of each of the three words is shot away, removed

explanation.surface: Wondering whether the great Brazilian can chip the keeper, every attempt leaves the coach lost for words.
explanation.walkthrough: Fabio Capello, Italian former England football manager, was mocked for his limited English, hence 'speechless'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabio Capello was the England football team's boss, famously sparing with words in English.

clue.text: Second person showing disapproval, s…say?

parts.note: someone who says tut-tut is a tutter

explanation.surface: Another disapproving speaker hesitates over their words.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition demonstrates itself: 's…say' is the stammered word.
explanation.definitionFit: The stammered s…say shows speech with repeated initial sounds, an example of the impediment.
